target_customer: Hardware teams needing small run plastic parts quickly
problem: Going from prototype to injection molded production parts takes weeks and expensive steel tooling, which blocks small runs.
business_model: Manufacturing services with instant quotes on prototype parts and production runs

founders.name: Oliver Johnson
education: Dropped out of college (institution not named)
founders.background_notes: Ran a 3D print farm and a college makerspace per YC page.

founders.name: Justin Kwon
education: Dropped out of college (institution not named)

technical_complexity.rationale: Printed photopolymer tooling that survives molding cycles with 48 hour turnaround needs materials and process development plus factory operations.

defensibility.rationale: Process know-how and speed could be hard to match, but 3D printed tooling is a known approach sold by others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents offer rapid tooling; no source shows them matching 48 hour production molding.

market_need_then: Hardware startups value fast iteration and domestic production; the company reports 500 kg of parts in its first month, unverified.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short, confident, technical; Fast plastics. Made in the USA.

brand_strength.rationale: Sinter is a manufacturing term that fits, but it is shared by several 3D printing firms such as Sinterit and Sintratec and no brand coverage exists.

outcome_analysis: Sinter is a two person Fall 2026 manufacturing startup with no exit and no verified funding. Its speed claims are unverified and hardware capital needs are high, so the outcome depends on proving repeatable production economics.
notes: Funding aggregators disagree and no company or press source confirms any round, so no round is recorded. No funding figure found by any search.
